video_title: Why Base Is Close to Calling Itself 'the Blockchain for Agent Finance
gist: Base head Jesse Pollock reports week-over-week growth across trading, payments and financing — tokenized equities above $1B weekly volume, Base passing Solana as the #2 on-chain lending market, and x402 agent micropayments for inference and data — after shipping 200ms blocks and the B20 RWA token standard. He says Base is close to repositioning as 'the blockchain for agent finance', plans a US tokenized-equities launch under the SEC innovation exemption, and is in no rush on a Base token.

themes.theme: Base growth metrics across trading, payments, financing

insights.claim: Jesse Pollock says that in the four months since he refocused on the Base chain, Base has grown week over week on all core metrics across trading, payments, financing and agents, driven by technical upgrades, new products and a sharper go-to-market.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Base activity momentum is a direct read on Coinbase's on-chain revenue lines; track weekly Base volume/TVL dashboards.
insights.quote: base is now growing basically week over week on all the core metrics that we care about

insights.claim: Tokenized equities on Base, a product that did not exist four months earlier, have crossed $1 billion of weekly trading volume.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Rapid traction for on-chain stocks suggests a new fee/volume source for Base and Coinbase and a growing RWA category to watch.
insights.quote: tokenized equities, uh, which just crossed a billion dollars of weekly volume

insights.claim: Base has overtaken Solana to become the second-largest on-chain financing (lending/borrowing) market after Ethereum, covering BTC/ETH-collateralized borrowing, USDC lending and business borrowing.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Shifting DeFi lending market share between L1s/L2s matters for relative positioning of SOL vs Base-exposed assets; verify with lending TVL data.
insights.quote: we just crossed Salana and are now the second biggest financing market on chain after Ethereum

insights.claim: About four weeks after launch, roughly $30 million of tokenized equities are being borrowed on Base, showing that Base's existing DeFi economy is absorbing tokenized stocks as a new collateral/asset class.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Composability of tokenized stocks with DeFi lending is an early signal of leverage on equities moving on-chain.
insights.quote: now have something like $30 million of tokenized equities borrowed

insights.claim: Base processes billions of dollars of payments volume every month and remains the preferred rail for USDC, with a growing share driven by agents.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: USDC payment flow concentration on Base links Coinbase's USDC economics to Base adoption.
insights.quote: base continues to be, you know, the preferred rail basically for USDC

insights.claim: FX trading — swapping dollar stablecoins against non-dollar stablecoins — is becoming a bigger and bigger trading category on Base alongside crypto majors and tokenized equities.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Non-USD stablecoin FX is an emerging on-chain market; watch for growth in EUR/other stablecoin issuers and FX venues on Base.

insights.claim: Pollock claims Base now has the most liquid Bitcoin, Ethereum and other crypto-major spot markets and the most liquid, highest-volume tokenized equities markets on-chain.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A liquidity-leadership claim worth verifying against DEX volume data; if true, it supports wallets and brokers routing to Base by default.
insights.quote: We now have the most liquid Bitcoin, Ethereum, other crypto major spot markets

themes.theme: Agentic payments via x402 and the 'agent finance' pivot

insights.claim: In roughly the last six weeks, Base found product-market fit for what agents buy with X42 (x402): inference and data, with agents making 1-2 cent micropayments for compute and for trading data on equities or tokens.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Inference and data are the first proven agent-payment use cases; watch x402 transaction counts and providers selling compute/data per call.
insights.quote: agents are using X42 to make micro payments for either acquiring trading data like information on equities or tokens um or to pay directly for their inference

insights.claim: Base's guiding belief is that AI agents will be the majority of actors in the global economy within the next few years, so it is redesigning the chain to be 'agent first'.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Signals Base's roadmap priority; infrastructure for agent wallets, micropayments and agent trading is where Base will concentrate effort.
insights.quote: we think that agents are going to be the majority of actors in the new global economy over the next few years

insights.claim: Base is close to rebranding its positioning from 'the blockchain for global finance' to 'the blockchain for agent finance', because it expects much of money movement to be driven by agents — both human-deployed and sovereign economic agents.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A positioning shift toward AI-agent commerce could attract agent-focused builders and narrative flows to Base ecosystem assets.
insights.quote: instead of calling base the blockchain for global finance, we want to say the blockchain for agent finance

insights.claim: Agentic finance is growing on Base as users deploy agents to run trading strategies in equities and spot crypto and to do high-frequency market making and searching.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Agent-driven trading increases on-chain volume and latency sensitivity, reinforcing the value of fast blocks.

insights.claim: Base's thesis is that the frontier-model 'single player' monopoly will give way to teams of agents built on open models that collaborate and can outpace frontier models, the way a team of people can outpace the smartest individual.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: If correct, value could shift from closed frontier labs toward open-model ecosystems and agent coordination/marketplace layers.
insights.quote: a team of agents may be able to outpace the smartest agent

insights.claim: Pollock argues the open marketplace for agents will naturally emerge on-chain because agents, being programmable, gravitate to programmable money; Base plans to talk much more about this 'agentic market' in 2027.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Expect 2027 Base announcements around agent marketplaces; a potential catalyst for agent-related tokens and Base ecosystem projects.
insights.quote: agents naturally gravitate towards programmable money because they are programmable themselves

themes.theme: Chain tech: own stack, 200ms blocks and the B20 token standard

insights.claim: At the start of the year Base took control of its technology stack, moving off a separate open-source stack onto its own stack (first upgrade, called Azul, in February or March) to specialize the chain for trading, payments and financing.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Base diverging from a shared open-source L2 stack implies faster, Base-specific features and less dependence on external roadmaps.

insights.claim: Base has done four upgrades this year, plans a fifth before year-end, and hopes to ship around 20 upgrades next year — roughly one every other week.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: An aggressive shipping cadence is a competitive edge versus slower L1/L2 governance cycles; monitor whether it delivers.
insights.quote: Uh next year I hope we'll have something like 20

insights.claim: Base cut block times from 2 seconds to 200 milliseconds, a 10x improvement aimed at latency-sensitive market makers, searchers and high-frequency traders who found the previous partial solution insufficient.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Faster blocks improve on-chain market quality and can pull HFT/market-making flow from competing chains.
insights.quote: Before it used to be 2cond blocks. Now it's 200 milliseconds.

insights.claim: B20 is Base's ERC-20-equivalent token standard for real-world assets, giving issuers built-in compliance, privacy, memo and ISO primitives for stablecoins, tokenized equities and private funds; tokens on B20 have already seen billions of dollars of trading volume.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A native RWA standard lowers issuance friction and may make Base the default venue for tokenization platforms.

insights.claim: Base says it will not compete with tokenization platforms; B20 is meant to strip out complexity so third-party tokenization platforms can bring assets to market more easily.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Tokenization platforms are positioned as partners, not rivals — favorable for platforms that integrate with Base.
insights.quote: the B20 isn't a tokenization platform. We're not going to go and compete

themes.theme: Tokenized equities: structure, regulation and US launch

insights.claim: Base's tokenized equities were deliberately slower to market so they could be 1:1, fully backed, free of debt-instrument structures and carry the rights of underlying shares, built with Coinbase on a tokenization standard for trusted equities.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Structure (direct backing vs debt/derivative wrappers) is a key differentiator among tokenized-stock offerings; it affects regulatory risk.
insights.quote: didn't have any weird debt structures in it that actually gave people the rights of the underlying shares

insights.claim: Base announced a collaboration with Broadridge to standardize on-chain shareholder voting and dividends that plug directly into its tokenized equities and that others can build on.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Broadridge's involvement (governance plumbing for US equities) lends TradFi legitimacy to on-chain stocks; watch BR for tokenization-related revenue.

insights.claim: Demand for Base's tokenized equities is coming strongly from retail outside the United States, where many people lack access to traditional equities.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Offshore retail access to US stocks is the current growth driver; regional demand is a leading indicator for global tokenized-stock volume.
insights.quote: we're seeing an incredible retail demand from outside the United States

insights.claim: The current tokenized equities on Base launched offshore before the SEC's innovation exemption; with that exemption in place, Coinbase/Base plans to bring the product to the United States and will share more in the coming months.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A US launch of tokenized equities would be a notable catalyst for Coinbase (COIN) and Base volume; watch for announcements in coming months.
insights.quote: with the SEC creating that innovation exemption, we're also really excited to bring it to the United States

insights.claim: Pollock says meetings with the SEC and CFTC are 'night and day' compared with before, with the agencies now engaging in good faith to use tokenization to unlock US capital markets innovation.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A friendlier US regulatory posture lowers risk for tokenization and crypto-native financial products.
insights.quote: it it it is like night and day

insights.claim: The B20-based tokenized equities currently on Base are fully permissionless and free-floating (not issued with issuer permission), with about 250 assets listed — more than any other venue, according to Pollock.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Permissionless listing of stocks without issuer consent is a scaling advantage but also a source of issuer pushback and regulatory risk.
insights.quote: the B20 version uh that is currently out there is fully permissionless

insights.claim: Pollock says issuers show hesitancy toward tokenization and that moving too fast or too broadly without education backfires; Coinbase prefers a measured, slow-and-steady approach even if competitors get ahead (alluding to the OKX/ICE controversy and public-company CEO pushback).
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Issuer resistance to unauthorized tokenized stocks is a real friction; Coinbase is positioning as the trusted, compliant alternative.
insights.quote: our approach with uh Coinbase has always been to um be measured to to be uh uh slow and steady even if it means that sometimes people are out ahead of us

insights.claim: Tokenized equities can let companies know their holders, pay dividends, grant voting rights and enable new programs like equity rewards and equity giveaways that were previously impossible.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: New corporate use cases (equity rewards) could be a pitch to issuers and expand the tokenized-stock market.

themes.theme: TradFi convergence and product-first distribution strategy

insights.claim: Pollock says it became clear in the last ~18 months that crypto has strong product-market fit for financial services (trading, payments, financing), which is why players from every side are now converging on the technology.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Competition for on-chain finance will intensify among chains, exchanges and TradFi; network effects and liquidity become decisive.
insights.quote: crypto has incredible product market fit for financial services

insights.claim: Base's strategy is product-centric rather than chasing splashy pre-announced name-brand TradFi partnerships (contrasting with deals such as ICE with Trade XYZ/Hyperliquid and LayerZero/DTCC/Citadel), betting that buyers choose the venue with best liquidity, cheapest borrowing and highest yields.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Announcements may not equal usage; judge chain competition by actual liquidity and volume rather than partnership headlines.
insights.quote: rather than doing kind of like pre-announced name brand flashy partnerships

insights.claim: Through Coinbase, Citi can now accept USDC on Base directly into business bank accounts, using the Coinbase Developer Platform.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: A major bank accepting USDC on Base is concrete TradFi adoption of stablecoin rails; supports USDC/Base payment volume growth.
insights.quote: now if you're a business on City, you can actually accept stable coins on base

insights.claim: Pollock frames the next phase of crypto adoption as two parallel paths: new agentic-finance entrants building fast-growing products, and incumbent institutions with distribution and assets using the technology to become more efficient.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Useful lens for sourcing: back both new agent-native fintechs and incumbents integrating stablecoin rails.

insights.claim: Base aims to be an exchange-like platform that any wallet, broker, neobank or neobrokerage can plug into, expecting all wallets — not just Coinbase Wallet — to gravitate to Base on product merit; it is already working with pump.fun on rewards for trading Base assets.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Base as neutral back-end liquidity layer means Base usage can grow independent of Coinbase's own front-end share.
insights.quote: almost like exchange- like platform where any wallet or any broker or any NEO bank or any NEO brokerage can plug in

insights.claim: The Base app was handed to Kobe and rebranded back to Coinbase Wallet, which is adding non-Base chains and products; Pollock now focuses solely on the Base chain.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: Decoupling the wallet from Base reduces captive distribution, so Base must win flow on infrastructure quality.

themes.theme: Base token: still exploring, no rush

insights.claim: Over a year after announcing it would explore a Base token, Base has made no decision and is 'not in a rush', prioritizing accelerating current growth while seeing a token as a potential lever for decentralization and aligning ecosystem participants.
insights.speaker: Jesse Pollock (head of Base)
insights.so_what: No near-term Base token catalyst; airdrop speculation should be discounted in the near term.
insights.quote: continuing to explore but also not being in a rush
